messages:
laura: quick follow-up to the CP separation RFC — we need to decide heartbeat / liveness semantics for agents when connected over private links (VPC peering, PrivateLink, VPN). Can we avoid spurious failovers and noisy control-plane load?

sanjay: +1. biggest constraints: NAT/idle timeouts, per-tenant egress churn, and limited control-plane scale for millions of tiny pings.

maria: my preference: keep a single persistent bidi gRPC stream from agent -> control-plane and piggyback health on it. application-level ping every 30s, with stream-level tcp keepalive tuned. that avoids extra calls.

kevin: careful with relying solely on TCP keepalive — cloud providers TTLs / NAT mappings can drop idle connections sooner than TCP defaults. we saw AWS NAT / ALB drop after ~350s with default cfg.

ethan: also think about PrivateLink: it can preserve source address differently and sometimes hides client ip, which hurts our per-agent metrics. we should emit agent_id with heartbeats so control-plane can map correctly.

laura: agreed. tradeoffs to call out:
- persistent-stream: fewer requests, easier to auth and multiplex, but susceptible to long idle/drop and expensive reconnect storms if many agents reconnect at once.
- separate heartbeat call (HTTP/gRPC unary): explicit TTL, simpler to reason about, but increases RPS on control-plane and may be blocked by peering NAT rules or rate-limits.

maria: proposal: hybrid model: maintain persistent stream for control traffic + light application-level heartbeat on the stream (every 30s). add a fallback unary heartbeat with exponential backoff used only after stream fails to reconnect within 10s.

kevin: +1 for hybrid. we should also jitter heartbeats by agent-id hash to avoid thundering herd on reconnect after maintenance. and use staggered reconnect windows.

laura: what about liveness semantics? we currently mark agent unhealthy after 3 missed pings (30s interval -> 90s). is that too aggressive across VPNs with variable latency?

sanjay: for private links I suggest tuning to 5 missed pings (150s) and adjust per-deployment via config. default 3 for hosted, 5 for private.

ethan: add a safety margin: when agents reconnect, control-plane should avoid immediate teardown of routes; use a soft-state TTL plus a 30s grace where traffic can be queued or routed to fallback. prevents brief flaps from breaking tenant traffic.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling agent canary 0.9.3 started in staging :rocket:

maria: auth note: heartbeats must be mTLS-protected or bearer-signed and include agent certificate serial to prevent spoofing if peering exposes connectivity broadly.

laura: implementation checklist I propose:
1) implement application heartbeat on existing bidi gRPC stream (30s interval, jittered).
2) add unary heartbeat fallback with exponential backoff and a 10s quick-reconnect window.
3) tune default missed-pings: hosted=3, private=5; make configurable per-deployment.
4) add reconnect jitter algorithm: hash(agent_id) % 60s window.
5) control-plane: on reconnect, mark as healthy but keep route state for 30s to avoid blackholes.
6) update RFC with wire format example and failure-mode diagrams.

kevin: also add an observability dashboard: metric for heartbeat rtt, reconnect rate, failed-auth-count; alert when reconnect rate spikes 3x baseline.

laura: +1. any objections?

sanjay: none from me. we should do an experiment two ways: simulate NAT drop by killing idle connections and test reconnect storm, and also test long-tail VPN latency.

maria: I can run the reconnect-storm sim in staging next week. will add a small load test harness.

laura: thanks. I’ll update the RFC and add the checklist + config knobs. tagging follow-ups: @maria please add test plan, @kevin add dashboard panels, @ethan validate auth changes with secops.

laura: example heartbeat payload for the RFC (very small):
```json
{"type":"heartbeat","agent_id":"a-123","ts":2723456789,"cert_sn":"AB:CD:EF","rtt_ms":42}
```

laura: ok will circulate updated RFC by EOD. if anyone has strong objections ping me here. :thumbsup:
